summary: **For Review Petitioner** : Shri Shubham Arya, Advocate, PGCIL Ms. Reeha Singh, Advocate, PGCIL Shri S. Vallinayagam, Advocate, TANGEDCO Ms. Supriya Singh, PGCIL Shri Arjun Malhotra, PGCIL Ms. Kirti, PGCIL - _b) Allow the review petition and modify the order dated 30.05.2024 passed in Petition No. 193/TT/2023 to the extent stated in the present review petition; and_ - _c) Pass any such further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem just and proper in the circumstances of the case.”_ - c. The time over-run on account of unforeseen uncontrollable events is not attributable to the Review Petitioner, and qualifies as an uncontrollable factor in terms of Regulation 22 and the same ought to be condoned by this Commission. Therefore, the Review Petitioner is entitled to IDC and IEDC. - a) The Review Petition is not maintainable in law and does not satisfy the settled principles governing exercise of review jurisdiction. The scope of review is limited by Order 47, Rule 1 of CPC. The Review Petitioner has not brought forth any new evidence that was unavailable during the original proceedings. Instead, the Review Petitioner reiterates arguments that were already considered and addressed by the Commission in the order dated 30.5.2025. It is a well-settled legal principle that - d) The issues raised by the Review Petitioner in the original tariff Petition and now reiterated in the Review Petition have already been heard and deliberated in detail in the Commission’s order dated 30.5.2024. The Review Petitioner is effectively seeking to re-argue the case on its merits, which amounts to an appeal in disguise and is not permissible in a review. - e) The Review Petitioner has merely referred to the records of the original tariff Petition No. 193/TT/2023 to claim an error apparent, yet no new facts or evidence have been presented that would warrant a review of the well-reasoned final order dated 30.05.2024 in Petition No. 193/TT/2023. 10. In response to the Commission queries vide Record of Proceeding of the hearings dated 23.4.2025 and 23.12.2025, the Review Petitioner has placed on record the Compliance Affidavit dated 26.11.2022 pertaining to the CEA Energization Certificate and the CEA Energization Certificate. The Review Petitioner has further submitted that the 20-day period, i.e., from 26.11.2022 to 16.12.2022, was consumed in obtaining the requisite charging codes from SRLDC to conduct the trial operation of the transmission asset. The Review Petitioner has reiterated the submissions regarding the time over-run in the instant Review Petition in the written submissions dated 9.1.2026. The Review Petitioner has further relied upon the APTEL’s judgments dated (a) 9.5.2019 in Appeal No. 125 of 2017, NTPC Limited v. CERC and Others and 7.10.2022 in Appeal No. 333 of 2022 (Tamil Nadu Generation and Distribution Corporation Limited v. CERC & Ors.), the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s judgment dated 10.1.2005 in Appeal (Civil) Nos. 237-239 of 2005 (Board of Cricket, India & Anr. v. Netaji Cricket Club & Ors.), and the APTEL’s judgment dated 8.11.2024 in Review Petition No. 03 of 2024 in Appeal No. 383 of 2022 (Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam Limited & Ors. v. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission & Ors). of “reviewing its decision, directions and orders”. Regulation 52(2) of the 2023 CBR provides the following grounds on which an aggrieved person can seek a review of a direction, decision or order of the Commission, which are akin to the grounds provided in Order 47 Rule 1 of CPC: _(2) Any person aggrieved by a direction, decision, or order of the Commission, from which no appeal has been preferred, may file a review petition on the following grounds within forty days of the making of such decision, direction, or order:_ 12. In the present case, the Review Petitioner has sought the review of the impugned order on the grounds of error apparent on the face of the record and oversight of relevant and material facts, which are dealt with in the subsequent paragraphs. 16. Before we examine the contentions of the Review Petitioner, we think it appropriate 17. The head-wise contentions submitted by the Review Petitioner in the instant Review Petition are analysed in the following paragraphs.: - ➢ _Thereafter, an order for compliance is issued by CEA usually within 1 week of inspection._ 23. Therefore, in view of the above deliberations, we are of the view that the Review Petitioner required some minimum time to respond to the observations through a compliance report and similarly, the CEA also requires some time to conduct the inspection and follow the procedure for issuance of Energization Certificate. Therefore, 30. It is a settled position in terms of the judgment of Hon`ble Supreme Court in Parsion Devi v. Sumitra Devi reported in 1997 8 SCC 715 that the review proceedings are not by way of an appeal and have to be strictly confined to the scope and ambit of Order 47 Rule 1 of CPC and that the judgment may be open to review, inter alia, if there is a mistake or an error apparent on the face of the record and that an error which is not self-evident and has to be detected by a process of reasoning can hardly be said to be an error apparent requiring court to exercise its power of review. The Hon'ble Supreme Court also enunciated these principles in judgment in Kamlesh Verma v. Mayawati and Ors., as reported in AIR 2006 SC 75. 33. For the reasons mentioned above, we find no substance in the contentions and the grounds urged by the Review Petitioner as the same are directed against the reasoning and conclusions recorded in the order seeking re-appreciation of the material on record and a different conclusion, which deserve to be rejected and hence rejected. 34. Accordingly, Review Petition No. 30/RP/2024 (in Petition No. 193/TT/2023) is disposed of in terms of the above discussions and findings.
